title: Vanishing on a principal open gives power torsion on a compact open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent], and $W\subseteq X$ a quasi-compact open. Let $a\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)$ and $t\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal F)$. Write $D_W(a)$ for the open of $W$ on which the germ of $a$ is invertible. If $t|_{D_W(a)}=0$, then $a^n t=0$ for some integer $n\geq0$. No quasi-separatedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01LC, proof; original proof steps 2-3, injectivity of principal localization of the finite section equalizer

proof.text: Choose finitely many affine opens U_i covering W by quasi-compactness and the affine-open basis. Restrict a and t to U_i. By affine quasi-coherent/tilde correspondence and principal-open localization, the restriction of t to D(a|U_i) is zero, so some power of a|U_i kills t|U_i. The equality D(a|U_i)=U_i cap D(a) and composition of restrictions transfer the given vanishing. In Lean the already proved affine result is exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_isAffineOpen.

Take the maximum N of the finitely many exponents (N=0 for an empty cover). For every i, multiply the local zero equality by the remaining power a^(N-n_i). Then (a^N t)|U_i=0. The uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom gives a^N t=0.
